title: Write a one-step equation with a variable for a problem (4 + x = 15)

lesson.title: Turning a Story into an Equation

steps.say: You already know that an equation is like a balance scale, and that the box in something like box plus four equals fifteen stands for a number we do not know yet. Today we do one small new thing: instead of drawing a box, we write a letter, and we build that equation ourselves from a story.

visual.caption: The box just gets a new name: x

steps.say: Here is our story. You are at the corner store in Victoria. You already have four dollars in your pocket, and your grandma gives you some more money. Now you have fifteen dollars altogether. We do not know how much grandma gave you, so we give that mystery amount a letter. Let us call it x. Four dollars plus x dollars is fifteen dollars, so we write four plus x equals fifteen.

visual.caption: The two parts together make 15 dollars

steps.say: Watch how the story turns into the equation, piece by piece. The four dollars you had becomes four. The word and, meaning put together, becomes the plus sign. The mystery money becomes x. And altogether I have fifteen becomes equals fifteen. So the whole sentence becomes four plus x equals fifteen. Notice we are only writing the equation right now, not solving it.

visual.caption: Left side and right side weigh the same

steps.say: Now here is a mistake lots of kids make, and I want you to spot it. Some kids read the equals sign as here comes the answer. So for eight plus four equals box plus five, they look at eight plus four, get twelve, and write twelve in the box. But that would mean twelve plus five, which is seventeen, and seventeen is not twelve. The scale tips over. The equals sign really means both sides weigh the same. Eight plus four is twelve, so the other side must also be twelve, and seven plus five is twelve. So the box is seven.

visual.caption: Writing 12 in the box makes the right side too heavy

steps.say: So when you build an equation from a story, ask yourself two questions. What am I not told? That becomes the letter. And what do both sides have to weigh the same? That goes on either side of the equals sign. For our store story, four plus x equals fifteen.

visual.caption: A balanced equation, ready to solve later

lesson.answer: Name the unknown with a letter, then write what balances: 4 + x = 15.

practice.question: Maya is filling her water bottle for soccer practice. She already has three hundred millilitres of water in it, and she pours in some more. Now the bottle holds seven hundred and fifty millilitres. Use the letter x for the amount she poured in, and write a one-step equation for this story. You do not need to solve it, but you may draw a balance scale to help you.
practice.answer: 300 + x = 750 (and if you want to check: x is 450 millilitres, because 300 plus 450 equals 750)
